subject: Re: Hummingbird PoC — 50ms p95 target, streaming behavior, and cost tradeoffs
messages:
From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
To: Dana Park <dana.park@hummingbird.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hummingbird PoC — latency targets & streaming behavior (post-call recap)

Hey Dana — great conversation today, thanks for the context. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the PoC kickoff.

Recap of requirements (from our call):
- Latency: target ~50ms p95 for single-turn chat (goal), acceptable up to 75ms p95 for initial PoC.
- Streaming: need early token delivery — first token ideally <30–40ms for interactive UX, with subsequent tokens steady.
- Throughput/concurrency: expected steady-state ~150–250 qps for concurrent sessions; burst up to ~500 qps during peak minutes.
- Prompts & tokens: mean prompt ~60 tokens, average reply ~120 tokens; some long tails to ~600 tokens.
- Availability: want fallbacks if the preferred GPU pool is constrained; regional routing in us-east preferred.

Preliminary cost/performance levers we'll evaluate:
- Continuous batching (keep batch windows tight, target 8–12ms additional batch latency cap).
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and common prefixes.
- Two model variants: a quantized LLM (q4_0-like) for cost-efficient baseline and a fp16 variant for tighter latency/quality tradeoffs.
- Adaptive routing: lower-cost model for non-critical traffic, fallback to higher-cost model for p95 violations.

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Confirm the 50ms p95 goal as the short-term success metric (or confirm 75ms if that's more realistic).
2) Share a (sanitized) sample of typical session traces or one week of anonymized prompts so we can run representative microbenchmarks.
3) Add our staging CIDR to your allowlist (we'll provide IPs once you give the green light).

Attached is a short SLO matrix template (hummingbird_slo_matrix.xlsx) and our PoC setup guide.

Next steps I propose:
- If you confirm, our SE (Lauren) will run a perf qualification plan next week, produce expected latency/cost curves for the two model variants, and propose an initial config (batching, cache TTLs, quantization).
- We'll schedule a 45-minute technical kickoff (SE + Prod Eng + infra) to sort out access and sampling.

Thanks — I’ll block a few slots for next week and send a calendar invite after I hear from you.

— Rafael

Thanks Rafael — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can confirm a goal of 50ms p95 for the interactive use-case; if the cost delta is large we can accept 70–75ms p95 for phase 1 while we validate quality.
- Typical traffic profile: 70% short sessions (avg 30–80 tokens total), 25% medium (200–400 tokens), 5% long (500–1,000 tokens).
- Concurrency expectation: baseline 200 qps with spikes to ~450 qps during launches.
- Streaming: first-byte under 40ms is ideal for our front-end; we can tolerate slightly higher for long generative outputs.

On sampling/data: I'll have a sanitized session dump and representative prompt set ready by EOD Friday (will upload to the Drive link you provided).

On procurement/pricing: we need a ballpark cost estimate for two configurations (quantized variant + fp16 variant) to model our TCO for the PoC (1 month, ~100M tokens).

I'll introduce our infra lead (infra@hummingbird.ai) to coordinate allowlist and network details. Let's target an SE-led kickoff on Monday morning (US Eastern) if that works for your team.

Cheers,
Dana

Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed perf qualification plan & initial cost estimate

Hi Dana / Rafael — Lauren (solutions engineering) here. Thanks for the details — below is our proposed technical approach for the PoC and rough cost/latency expectations so Hummingbird can model tradeoffs.

1) Perf qualification plan (what we run in week 1):
- Microbenchmarks: synthetic prompt shapes matching your distribution (short/med/long) to measure first-byte and steady-state throughput for single-worker and multi-worker configs.
- End-to-end staging test: replay a sampled set of real anonymized prompts against a small staging fleet with streaming enabled to measure first-token latency and chunk pacing.
- Failure/fallback tests: simulate GPU pool pressure to validate routing and canary fallback behavior.

2) Key knobs we'll tune:
- Continuous batching: target batch latency cap = 8–12ms to keep utility of batching while protecting first-byte latency. We'll report p50/p95 p99 with and without batching.
- KV/prefix caching: TTLs starting at 15 minutes for common system prompts; this should significantly reduce compute for repeated initial prompts.
- Quantization profile: test a q4_0-like config (aggressive 4-bit) and a q8/q6 middle ground; compare to fp16 for quality/latency.
- Model variants: run redwood-medium-fp16 and redwood-large-q4 baseline; if quality gap is material, we may recommend mixed routing (cheap model for 80% traffic).

3) Initial expected numbers (very rough, for capacity planning):
- redwood-large-q4 (aggressive quant): first-byte 30–50ms p95 (with continuous batching cap), throughput per GPU ~6–8 rps for average 180-token responses; cost: ~ $1,200–$1,800 / 1M tokens (estimate for PoC env).
- redwood-medium-fp16 (higher perf): first-byte 20–35ms p95, throughput per GPU ~10–14 rps; cost: ~ $2,200–$2,800 / 1M tokens.

Notes on estimates: these are ballpark for PoC hardware in us-east, not committed pricing. We'll provide precise measured curves after the microbenchmarks.

4) Data/access required from Hummingbird:
- Staging allowlist for our test endpoints (we'll provide IPs).
- Upload of anonymized sample prompts (Drive link).
- Optional: a short run of production-mirrored traffic (1–2 hours at small scale) to validate real-world distribution — only if you are comfortable.

5) Deliverables by end of week:
- Latency vs cost curves for both model variants, recommendation for batching/cache/quantization TLDR, and a short runbook for the frontend integration (streaming knobs).

Action items:
- Dana: confirm sample upload timeline (you mentioned EOD Friday) and kickoff availability Monday morning ET.
- Rafael: will send calendar invite for Monday 9:30am ET; adding Ben for billing/contract questions.

Happy to iterate on the plan — can be more conservative on batching if you want stricter first-byte behavior.

— Lauren
